results.title: Demystifying OOM Killer in Kubernetes: Tracking Down Memory Issues | Cloud Native Daily
results.snippet: By sacrificing one process, the OOM killer prevents a complete system crash, ensuring the overall stability of the cluster. When a pod in Kubernetes exceeds its specified memory limit, it triggers an OOM event.

results.title: Kubernetes Pod vs. Container OOMKilled - Stack Overflow
results.snippet: If I understand correctly the conditions for Kubernetes to OOM kill a pod or container (from komodor.com): If a container uses more memory than its memory limit, it is terminated with an OOMKilled status.

results.title: 5 Ways You Can Diagnose & Prevent OOMKilled Errors in Kubernetes
results.snippet: In Kubernetes, there is an important difference between a container being OOMKilled because it exceeded its own cgroup memory limit and a container being OOMKilled during node-level memory exhaustion.

results.title: How to Fix OOMKilled Kubernetes Error (Exit Code 137)?
results.snippet: When a container attempts to consume more memory than its set limit the Linux OOM Killer changes the container status to ‘OOMKilled’, which prompts Kubernetes to terminate it. This mechanism prevents a single container from exhausting the node’s memory, which could compromise other containers running on the same node.
